change.scope: One additional resource-priced two-tree AllReduce candidate after mapping and original route refinement.
change.construction: At each level, merge at most four rank groups. Select a parent by switch-only directed rank-pair path prices for both reduction and broadcast. Reprice the first tree level loads on every edge and overlapping shared resource before generating the corresponding second-tree level.
change.direction: Reduction and broadcast directions are routed independently; a reverse physical edge is not assumed. Logical tree paths use separate rank transfers over successive rounds, never a rank as an intermediate path node.
change.partitions: Largest legal split, width 4, exactly three integer slot partitions: equal, first tree one quarter, first tree three quarters.
change.rounds: Two times ceil(log2(rank_count)/2); each whole slot belongs to one tree. Read start-of-round contributor state; reduce disjoint contributors; only copy complete sums.
change.prediction: Joint equal-demand multipath fractions for both trees per round, rounded separately for each tree slot count. Actual integer combined edge/resource traversal loads, repeated memberships, active-path overhead and transfer path cost use the Replay formula.
change.pipeline: Prepare two-tree plans after the original portfolio and mapping preparation during the same one-call model wait. After original selection/mapping/repair, screen against the refined original; at most one new complete tree schedule is built.
change.model_reply: Existing c proposals and optional m remain supported. Optional t: 0 disable, 1 equal, 2 first quarter, 3 first three quarters; omitted means minimum predicted cost. Original replies without t remain valid.
change.model_input: Current bytes, alignment, legal splits, directed link/capacity statistics, shared-resource bottlenecks, XOR profiles and initial seeds; eligible tree split/width/rounds/partitions explicitly marked not yet measured.
audit: prepare_dual_tree: generated tree edges, all three integer predictions and separated tree/route/prediction timings
evaluate_dual_tree: selected partition linked to model call, full costs and adoption
Existing model reply, input hash, original candidate evaluations, mapping, route repair and stage timings retained
change.failure_handling: Only expected AgentCCError construction failures become explicit unroutable candidate rejections. Full validation and programming errors propagate.
change.theory_limit: Heuristic tree packing and resource repricing, not full ForestColl or DualColl and no transferred throughput-optimality claim.

Legal split, allow_copy and round-limit eligibility; directed costs exclude rank intermediates

http_comparison.order: Two public repeats reverse version order per case; four mutation pairs, two mapping-control pairs and four tree-control pairs; one warmup pair excluded.
http_comparison.p95_method: Inclusive linear interpolation over 28 public HTTP requests per version.
http_comparison.variation_note: Small non-tree communication variations reflect the existing wall-clock route repair, not the two-tree method.

acceptance.communication: Fullmesh Clos AR improves 37.57 percent in both public repeats; other public tree candidates screened out.

offline_studies.initial_fanout_search: 2, 4 and 8 group merges explored outside runtime; all seven best schedules validated. Runtime uses only fanout 4 to bound work; fanout-8 Mesh2D gains are not shipped.

limitations: No real model, official hidden input or official Replay call was used. The user-reported best official version remains 0.2.3.
Public two-tree gains are concentrated in Fullmesh Clos AR. The shipped candidate did not improve Mesh2D AR or NVLink-like AR.
Mean HTTP overhead was 37.6 ms in this comparison, but P95 rose by 433.6 ms; two repeats do not establish a general latency guarantee.
The unchanged 100-ms wall-clock path repair is timing-sensitive. Small non-tree differences must not be credited to double trees.
Tree preparation may extend the critical path and may be discarded when the model disables the trial or selects an inferior ratio.
Joint route fractions optimize equal demands before integer slot scaling; unequal ratios are estimated exactly but not separately continuously optimized.
Only width 4 and the largest legal split are tried. No global tree-packing or throughput optimality is claimed.
Actual model token usage, model inference latency and total official score improvement remain unmeasured.
